description: Local compatibility patch carrier for the vendored Hermes gateway. Tracked in the autophagy repo, applied idempotently on deploy, reversible via backup.

patches.reason: pre_gateway_dispatch is only invoked in _handle_message; messages arriving during an active turn are queued and consumed by a recursive _run_agent continuation that never invokes the hook. This bypasses skill-generation observation (W6-4) and the meeting-gate fail-closed veto (W2-3). The patch invokes the hook exactly once at busy-entry (_handle_active_session_busy_message), guarded by an event.metadata marker; fail-safe (only an explicit skip drops).
patches.removal_condition: Remove once an upstream Hermes release invokes pre_gateway_dispatch for busy-path / queued follow-up messages (its documented 'fired once per incoming MessageEvent' contract).
patches.upstream_pr: TODO: submit upstream — pre_gateway_dispatch not fired on busy/continuation path

patches.reason: In busy_input_mode=queue, consecutive same-sender owner Discord DM text arriving during a long turn is newline-merged into ONE follow-up turn (the seam return False defers to base.py _flush_text_debounce_now -> merge_pending_message_event(merge_text=True)), mixing unrelated requests. This routes owner Discord DM text through relatedness-aware FIFO segmentation instead: UNRELATED -> separate sequential turns (arrival order in _pending_messages head + _queued_events overflow), RELATED (<=1.0s burst measured from the last physical DM, or reply-to-tail) -> merge into tail; the long task finishes uninterrupted (no interrupt/steer). Also: over-cap (>32) sends a rate-limited notice AND marks the rejected DM's receipt failed; the _MAX_INTERRUPT_DEPTH cap re-queues by prepend; each FIFO-drained follow-up turn finalizes its own per-physical-DM receipts (on_processing_complete only fires for the outer turn); and gateway start() reconciles any receipts left 'received' by a prior crash to failed. Fail-safe: any error defers to the original return False.
patches.runtime_deps: ~/.hermes/hermes-compat/hermes_compat_boot.py (flat) + ~/.hermes/hermes-compat/automation/hermes_compat/{owner_dm_relatedness,owner_dm_signal,owner_dm_dispatch,receipt_tracker,receipt_ledger,receipt_apply}.py; injected code imports via bootstrap (__path__ merge) + absolute automation.hermes_compat.*
patches.removal_condition: Remove once an upstream Hermes release segments queue-mode busy text per message (no newline-merge) with relatedness batching.
patches.upstream_pr: TODO: submit upstream — queue-mode busy text newline-merges unrelated messages

patches.reason: The 👀/✅/❌ receipt reaction attaches only to the message that STARTS a turn; merged/queued DMs get processed without any receipt. This (1) preserves ALL raw messages through the ingress text-batch merge, (2) adds 👀 at receipt to every physical owner DM, (3) resolves ✅/❌ per physical DM of the completing logical turn, with a content-free crash-visibility ledger (channel_id/message_id/state only). Fail-safe throughout.
patches.removal_condition: Remove once upstream Hermes gives a per-message receipt lifecycle for merged/queued messages.
patches.upstream_pr: TODO: submit upstream — receipt reaction is per-turn, not per-message

patches.reason: The gateway renders its own turn telemetry onto whatever surface the turn arrived on. In an owner DM that is a private operational view; in a Discord guild channel or thread it puts the agent's internal work process on a user-facing surface — token-streaming drafts, tool-progress lines carrying tool names and raw arguments, thinking/reasoning relay, context-pressure status callbacks, 'still working' heartbeats, and raw background-process output. This patch injects an event-typed, fail-closed allowlist: Discord DM stays private/unchanged, every other Discord chat_type (guild channel, auto-created thread, existing thread, unknown/new type) is public, and only final result / approval request / user question / failure summary / completion notification may be delivered there. Decisions are made by kind, never by scrubbing rendered strings. The single display-surface resolver (_display_surface_mode) is patched rather than its three call sites, so a visibility surface upstream adds later is denied on public Discord without a new patch. Deliberate deviation from the original workspace implementation: the agent-notify background branch is NOT blanked — it wakes the agent via an internal MessageEvent rather than delivering to chat, so blanking it would blind the agent while adding no privacy. Fail-CLOSED: when the carrier module is unreachable the injected helpers still recognise a public Discord surface and suppress.
patches.runtime_deps: ~/.hermes/hermes-compat/hermes_compat_boot.py (flat) + ~/.hermes/hermes-compat/automation/hermes_compat/public_message_policy.py; injected code imports via bootstrap (__path__ merge) + absolute automation.hermes_compat.public_message_policy, and falls back to an inline fail-closed surface check if that import fails
patches.removal_condition: Remove once an upstream Hermes release makes turn telemetry (streaming drafts, tool progress, reasoning relay, status callbacks, long-running heartbeats, background-process output) opt-in per surface class rather than per platform, with non-DM Discord defaulting to off.
patches.upstream_pr: TODO: submit upstream — display.platforms.discord settings cannot distinguish a 1:1 DM from a guild channel or thread

patches.reason: send_exec_approval is a public adapter method: plugins and recovery paths call it directly with whatever metadata they hold, so the gateway-side seam in discord-public-message-policy cannot be the only enforcement point. This re-checks at the adapter, where the resolved channel object is stronger evidence than any chat_type string — a Discord DM channel has guild None, while a guild channel and a thread inside one both have a guild, so anything not provably a DM is treated as public. The approval prompt and its buttons stay public (the owner must be able to act on it); only the requested command and the reason are replaced with an opaque protected-operation description. No import of the carrier module here on purpose: this path must keep working while the carrier is half-deployed.
patches.runtime_deps: none (self-contained; deliberately independent of the carrier import path)
patches.removal_condition: Remove together with discord-public-message-policy, or once upstream send_exec_approval takes a surface-visibility argument and withholds command/reason itself on non-DM surfaces.
patches.upstream_pr: TODO: submit upstream — send_exec_approval prints the raw command into guild channels

notes: hermes update overwrites the vendored install; re-run automation/hermes_compat/deploy.sh after any update.
Rebased v0.18.2 -> v0.20.3 on 2026-08-18 after an unrestored hermes-update autostash left all three patches off production since 2026-08-16. Each applier docstring records which seams moved.

patch state is machine-checkable: `python3 -m automation.hermes_compat.patch_state --install-root ~/.hermes/hermes-agent` exits 0 all-applied / 1 one or more missing / 2 undecidable. The note that used to sit here claimed automation/healthcheck.sh surfaced a missing patch; that file never mentioned this carrier at all, and all three patches ran off production for two days (2026-08-16~18) with nothing saying so. Wiring this probe into healthcheck is NOT done yet — do not read this note as if it were.
This carrier does NOT hard-block gateway startup; a fail-closed ExecStartPre gate is a deliberate opt-in next step (brick risk).
